precepts.text: There's a scripture that says days should speak, and multitude of years should show wisdom, but there's a spirit in man.
precepts.point: A brother: Which goes back to what you were saying. Remember, there's a scripture that says days should speak, and multitude of years should show wisdom, but there's a spirit in man. A lot of older brothers who lived from the time of the fifties and sixties, they amounted to nothing. But they want to be over men. But you have to study first. You have to learn God's laws and apply God's laws. But they feel because of their age they can be over younger men. No, you're not at that level yet. Spiritually, you're not growing. You're still at an infant stage. We don't care if you're eighty years old. If you don't know God's laws, you're an infant. You're a toddler according to the word of God. Everybody understand that?

note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

precepts.why:
Sirach says “The law shall be found perfect without lies”, and “A man that hath travelled knoweth many things; and he that hath much experience will declare wisdom.” It is talking about the man that knows the law and travels. Some of you were in the military and traveled, and you don't know nothing. Some of you are old and traveled here and there, and you don't know nothing, only because you don't know the law. Travel and years do not make wisdom without God's laws.

That goes back to Job 32: days should speak, and the multitude of years should show wisdom, but there is a spirit in man. A lot of older brothers who lived from the time of the fifties and sixties amounted to nothing, but they want to be over men. You have to study first. You have to learn God's laws and apply God's laws. They feel because of their age they can be over younger men. No, you are not at that level yet. Spiritually you are not growing; you are still at an infant stage. We don't care if you are eighty years old: if you don't know God's laws, you are an infant, a toddler, according to the word of God.

The understanding does not come from the number of years but from the spirit God puts in a man. Military men who have been to Syria and Iraq don't know what they are looking at, because they are not studied to know what to look for. The man whose years and travels are joined to the law is the one that declares wisdom.

precepts.text: That's why Paul told Timothy, let no man despise your youth.
precepts.point: A brother: Good point behind that. That's why Paul told Timothy, let no man despise your youth. Because God chose that man, Timothy, at that point, and he's going to be over some older men in age. And it doesn't make the older man less. But don't try to use your age and your worldly wisdom to think it's going to outshine God's wisdom. God's going to choose who he wants and where he wants them in his body. And that's just what it is. Just be glad that you part of this mission, and play your role.

note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

precepts.why:
That is why Paul told Timothy, let no man despise your youth. God chose that man, Timothy, at that point, and he was going to be over some men older than him in age.

It doesn't make the older man less. But don't try to use your age and your worldly wisdom as though it is going to outshine God's wisdom. God is going to choose who he wants and where he wants them in his body, and that is just what it is. Be glad that you are part of this mission, and play your role.

It fits what Sirach 34 says: “The law shall be found perfect without lies: and wisdom is perfection to a faithful mouth.” Wisdom is in the law and the faithful mouth, not in the gray hair. A young man who knows God's laws, keeps them and labors in them, teaching all them that seek learning, is not to be despised because of his youth; and an older man who never learned the law is still an infant, however many years he has.

precepts.text: Another word for teaching. You going out, and you start with an L. Luke 14:23.
precepts.point: You're teaching for who? Teaching our people. Teaching for the Lord. Okay. Where's that at? We're teaching for our people. Yeah. You close, because you teach. Another word for teaching. You going out, and you start with an L. Luke 14. Starts with an L. It has an A. It has an O. Labour. Okay. So you labouring for who? The Lord. Luke 14:23. Oh, you labour for who? You said before. For our people to wake up. Yeah. Okay. Tell me. You know what I'm talking about, sir? Let me hear.

note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

precepts.why:
“He that hath travelled is full of prudence. When I travelled, I saw many things”. Travelling doing what? Teaching. And another word for teaching, when you are going out, starts with an L: labour. That is Luke 14:23, the servant sent out by his lord. You are labouring for the Lord, for our people to wake up.

Sirach says the same of himself: “Consider that I laboured not for myself only, but for all them that seek learning.” You travel the world and seek out people that want to learn. But first you have to keep the commandments, learn and study, and then go out and teach. Military men travel too; they have been to Syria and Iraq, but they cannot tell you about Dura Europos or the walls of Cyrus. They travel, but they have not studied to know what to look for.

Judith shows why the labour matters: “Now therefore, O brethren, let us shew an example to our brethren, because their hearts depend upon us, and the sanctuary, and the house, and the altar, rest upon us.” The people are depending on us, so it is our job to study, get right, and travel to share the word with our people. Later somebody comes behind you, and you share your experience and teach them. That is part of how you go from milk to meat.

The labour brings experience you cannot get staying home. In Cuba the police came with nightsticks and a paddy wagon; teaching without a license there could bring two years in jail with no trial, and the police chief said this teaching would cause a revolution. Having gone through that, the brethren learned there is a different way to approach it, not to stop teaching there. That is why it is good to get around learned men who have travelled: they understand more than they can express in one conversation.

And the one who labours for the Lord is kept by him: “I was ofttimes in danger of death: yet I was delivered because of these things.” “Whoso feareth the Lord shall not fear nor be afraid; for he is his hope.” If you are sincere in this truth and really keeping his commandments, that spirit will come on you and you will not fear. They said nobody could go up into Laventille in Trinidad because of the gangs; the brethren went up there to teach, and it put a spirit on those men, and now they go up there.

precepts.text: The bread of the needy is their life: he that defraudeth him thereof is a man of blood; he that taketh away his neighbour's living slayeth him. What Simon did was no light thing. Taking money from the widows, the orphans, the fatherless, and the strangers is murder; that was their livelihood. That is why it is never just one sin.
precepts.point: The high priest told him that there was such money laid up for the relief of widows and fatherless children, and that some of it belonged to Hircanus son of Tobias, a man of great dignity, and not as that wicked Simon had misinformed: in all four hundred talents of silver and two hundred of gold. And that it was altogether impossible that such wrong should be done unto them that had committed it to the holiness of the place.

note.label: From Brother To Betrayer

precepts.why:
Onias said there was money laid up for the relief of widows and fatherless children, “and not as that wicked Simon had misinformed”, and that it was “altogether impossible that such wrongs should be done unto them, that had committed it to the holiness of the place.”

There is a scripture that says keeping a man’s earnings from him is like murder: “The bread of the needy is their life: he that defraudeth him thereof is a man of blood. He that taketh away his neighbour’s living slayeth him; and he that defraudeth the labourer of his hire is a bloodshedder.”

What Simon did was no light thing. Taking money from the widows, the orphans, the fatherless and the strangers is murder. That was their livelihood; we took care of them with that money. Simon would rather have Esau come and take it all than help his own people. He is a murderer.

That is why it is never just one sin. All I did was tell them about the money? No, you did worse than you think. Sin is a domino effect: one hits the next and it goes all around. That is why Onias was in such agony, the priests lay on their faces before the altar and the whole city cried to heaven, and why the Lord of spirits sent the horse with the terrible rider and the two young men to scourge Heliodorus.

precepts.text: Dreams lift up fools; whoso regardeth dreams is like him that catcheth at a shadow. Don't chase dreams. But verse 3 gives you a clue to understanding dreams from God: the vision of dreams is the resemblance of one thing to another, even as the likeness of a face to a face. You could dream about somebody you know, but it's not them; it's someone similar, in age or in what they do. You just have to know the people in your circle.
precepts.point: Yet did not the chief butler remember Joseph, but forgat him.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
The butler and the baker of the king of Egypt offended their lord and were put in ward “the place where Joseph was bound.” “they dreamed a dream both of them, each man his dream in one night,” and in the morning they were sad, because “there is no interpreter of it.” Joseph answered, “Do not interpretations belong to God? tell me them, I pray you.”

Sirach speaks to dreams: “The hopes of a man void of understanding are vain and false: and dreams lift up fools.” “Whoso regardeth dreams is like him that catcheth at a shadow, and followeth after the wind.” Don't chase dreams; a man who lives by every dream is grasping at shadows.

But verse 3 gives a clue to understanding the dreams that come from God: “The vision of dreams is the resemblance of one thing to another, even as the likeness of a face to a face.” You may dream about somebody you know, say a man named Joe, and see Joe's face; but it is not Joe. It is someone similar to Joe, maybe in age or in what they do for a living. It could be Bob. You just have to know the people in your circle.

That is how the dreams in Genesis 40 work. The butler's vine with “three branches” and the baker's “three white baskets” were resemblances of one thing to another: the three branches and the three baskets were three days. The interpretation belonged to God, and Joseph gave it.

precepts.text: Nor for the pestilence that walketh in darkness, nor for the destruction that wasteth at noonday.
precepts.point: Habakkuk 3:16, the prophet's belly trembled because he was put in it, and when he cometh up unto the people he will invade them with his troops. Isaiah 31:4, like as the lion and the young lion roaring on his prey, the Lion of the tribe of Judah of Revelation 5:5, so shall the Lord of hosts come down to fight for mount Zion; as birds flying, Christ and the angels, he will defend Jerusalem, and passing over he will preserve it. Jeremiah 4:7, the lion is come up from his thicket, the destroyer of the Gentiles, Nebuchadnezzar contextually and Christ prophetically. 2 Esdras 11:37, a roaring lion chased out of the wood sends a man's voice unto the eagle, America.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
“For the eyes of the Lord are upon them that love him, he is their mighty protection and strong stay, a defence from heat, and a cover from the sun at noon”. God's eyes are on them that love him, and he is our mighty protection if we love him. A defence from what heat? Nuclear heat. And why a cover from the sun at noon? Because the destruction comes at noonday.

David shows it: “Nor for the pestilence that walketh in darkness; nor for the destruction that wasteth at noonday.” The destruction wastes at noonday.

So all we have to do is be faithful and fear him, and he will protect us from the destruction to come. Sirach says the same of wisdom: “By her he shall be covered from heat, and in her glory shall he dwell.” By wisdom we shall be covered from the heat.

precepts.text: The righteous man stands in great boldness before those who afflicted him; they are troubled with terrible fear and amazed at the strangeness of his salvation, so far beyond all they looked for.
precepts.point: Habakkuk 3:16, the prophet's belly trembled because he was put in it, and when he cometh up unto the people he will invade them with his troops. Isaiah 31:4, like as the lion and the young lion roaring on his prey, the Lion of the tribe of Judah of Revelation 5:5, so shall the Lord of hosts come down to fight for mount Zion; as birds flying, Christ and the angels, he will defend Jerusalem, and passing over he will preserve it. Jeremiah 4:7, the lion is come up from his thicket, the destroyer of the Gentiles, Nebuchadnezzar contextually and Christ prophetically. 2 Esdras 11:37, a roaring lion chased out of the wood sends a man's voice unto the eagle, America.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
The Lord is a defence from heat for them that love him, and in that day they will stand. “Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.” Why does he stand in boldness? Because he feared the Lord and stayed faithful.

“When they see it, they shall be troubled with terrible fear”. When the nations see it they will be troubled, saying, what the hell is this? They “shall be amazed at the strangeness of his salvation, so far beyond all that they looked for.” They cannot imagine it; they will not be able to fathom what is taking place when those chariots come.

“And they repenting and groaning for anguish of spirit shall say within themselves, This was he, whom we had sometimes in derision, and a proverb of reproach: We fools accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honour: How is he numbered among the children of God, and his lot is among the saints!”

The ones who mocked and afflicted the righteous will see him numbered among the children of God, protected while they are not.

precepts.text: Behold, he cometh with clouds, and every eye shall see him, and all kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him.
precepts.point: Habakkuk 3:16, the prophet's belly trembled because he was put in it, and when he cometh up unto the people he will invade them with his troops. Isaiah 31:4, like as the lion and the young lion roaring on his prey, the Lion of the tribe of Judah of Revelation 5:5, so shall the Lord of hosts come down to fight for mount Zion; as birds flying, Christ and the angels, he will defend Jerusalem, and passing over he will preserve it. Jeremiah 4:7, the lion is come up from his thicket, the destroyer of the Gentiles, Nebuchadnezzar contextually and Christ prophetically. 2 Esdras 11:37, a roaring lion chased out of the wood sends a man's voice unto the eagle, America.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
The nations will be amazed at the strangeness of the salvation of the righteous, “so far beyond all that they looked for”, when those chariots come. John shows those chariots: “Behold, he cometh with clouds”. He is coming with clouds, and those clouds are his chariots.

And “every eye shall see him, and they also which pierced him: and all kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him.” Christ is returning with the multitude of angels, and all kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him.

That is the day the Lord is “a defence from heat, and a cover from the sun at noon” for them that love him: when every eye sees him coming, the righteous stand in boldness while the kindreds of the earth wail.

precepts.text: When I heard, my belly trembled; when he cometh up unto the people, he will invade them with his troops.
precepts.point: Habakkuk 3:16, the prophet's belly trembled because he was put in it, and when he cometh up unto the people he will invade them with his troops. Isaiah 31:4, like as the lion and the young lion roaring on his prey, the Lion of the tribe of Judah of Revelation 5:5, so shall the Lord of hosts come down to fight for mount Zion; as birds flying, Christ and the angels, he will defend Jerusalem, and passing over he will preserve it. Jeremiah 4:7, the lion is come up from his thicket, the destroyer of the Gentiles, Nebuchadnezzar contextually and Christ prophetically. 2 Esdras 11:37, a roaring lion chased out of the wood sends a man's voice unto the eagle, America.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
Christ is returning with clouds, with his chariots and the multitude of angels. Habakkuk saw it: “When I heard, my belly trembled; my lips quivered at the voice: rottenness entered into my bones, and I trembled in myself”. Why did he tremble? Because Habakkuk was put in it. He felt it; he saw it.

He trembled “that I might rest in the day of trouble: when he cometh up unto the people, he will invade them with his troops.” When Christ comes up unto the people, he will invade them with his troops, the angels.

That is the day of trouble in which the Lord is the mighty protection and strong stay of them that love him. The prophet trembled at what he saw, but those who fear the Lord will rest in that day.

precepts.text: Like as the lion roaring on his prey, so shall the Lord of hosts come down to fight for mount Zion; as birds flying, so will he defend Jerusalem, and passing over he will preserve it.
precepts.point: Habakkuk 3:16, the prophet's belly trembled because he was put in it, and when he cometh up unto the people he will invade them with his troops. Isaiah 31:4, like as the lion and the young lion roaring on his prey, the Lion of the tribe of Judah of Revelation 5:5, so shall the Lord of hosts come down to fight for mount Zion; as birds flying, Christ and the angels, he will defend Jerusalem, and passing over he will preserve it. Jeremiah 4:7, the lion is come up from his thicket, the destroyer of the Gentiles, Nebuchadnezzar contextually and Christ prophetically. 2 Esdras 11:37, a roaring lion chased out of the wood sends a man's voice unto the eagle, America.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
“For thus hath the Lord spoken unto me, Like as the lion and the young lion roaring on his prey”. What is this talking about? The Lion of the tribe of Judah in Revelation 5:5: Christ.

And “when a multitude of shepherds is called forth against him, he will not be afraid of their voice, nor abase himself for the noise of them: so shall the Lord of hosts come down to fight for mount Zion, and for the hill thereof.” The Lord is going to fight for his people.

“As birds flying, so will the Lord of hosts defend Jerusalem”. As birds flying is Christ and the angels. And “defending also he will deliver it; and passing over he will preserve it.” Passing over: this is the Passover season, and just as he passed over us in Egypt, he will pass over and preserve his people.

That is what it means that his eyes are upon them that love him and he is their mighty protection. He comes down as a roaring lion to fight for mount Zion and defend Jerusalem.

precepts.text: The Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, hath prevailed. That lion is Christ.
precepts.point: Habakkuk 3:16, the prophet's belly trembled because he was put in it, and when he cometh up unto the people he will invade them with his troops. note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
Isaiah says the Lord will come down to fight for mount Zion “Like as the lion and the young lion roaring on his prey”. Who is that lion? John shows it: “And one of the elders saith unto me, Weep not: behold, the Lion of the tribe of Juda, the Root of David, hath prevailed to open the book, and to loose the seven seals thereof.”

That lion is Christ, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David. He is the one roaring on his prey, not afraid of the voice of the multitude of shepherds called against him, coming down with his angels as birds flying to defend Jerusalem. He is the mighty protection of them that love him.

precepts.text: The lion is come up from his thicket, and the destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way to make thy land desolate, and thy cities laid waste without an inhabitant.
precepts.point: Habakkuk 3:16, the prophet's belly trembled because he was put in it, and when he cometh up unto the people he will invade them with his troops. Isaiah 31:4, like as the lion and the young lion roaring on his prey, the Lion of the tribe of Judah of Revelation 5:5, so shall the Lord of hosts come down to fight for mount Zion; as birds flying, Christ and the angels, he will defend Jerusalem, and passing over he will preserve it. note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
The lion that roars on his prey is Christ, and Jeremiah shows him coming: “The lion is come up from his thicket, and the destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way”. This is twofold. It was talking about Nebuchadnezzar contextually, but prophetically it is talking about Jesus the Christ. He's coming.

And “he is gone forth from his place to make thy land desolate; and thy cities shall be laid waste, without an inhabitant.” He comes forth from his place to make the land of the Gentiles desolate, their cities laid waste without inhabitants.

So while the destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way, the eyes of the Lord are upon them that love him, and he is their defence from the heat of that destruction.

precepts.text: As it were a roaring lion chased out of the wood sent out a man's voice unto the eagle. Christ roaring against America.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
The lion is Christ, roaring on his prey and coming up from his thicket as the destroyer of the Gentiles. Ezra saw the same lion: “And I beheld, and lo, as it were a roaring lion chased out of the wood: and I saw that he sent out a man’s voice unto the eagle”.

This eagle is America. The roaring lion sending his voice unto the eagle is Christ roaring against America, bringing destruction.

So when the destruction that wasteth at noonday comes on America, the Lord is the mighty protection of them that love him, a defence from heat and a cover from the sun at noon, while he roars against the eagle and fights for mount Zion.

precepts.text: The principal things for the whole use of man's life are water, fire, iron, salt, flour, honey, milk, wine, oil and clothing.
precepts.point: Economic violence is still violence, even without a sword.

note.label: Babylon Speaks Plainly: Venezuela and the Real WMD

precepts.why:
The curse says we would serve our enemies in hunger, thirst, nakedness and want of all things. Why does it target those things specifically? Sirach names the chief things in life: “The principal things for the whole use of man’s life are water, fire, iron, and salt, flour of wheat, honey, milk, and the blood of the grape, and oil, and clothing.”

When you target those things, you dehumanize people. You take away the principal things needful for life, for them to be dignified, and those things are robbed from them. That is why they will never let the resources in their so-called backyard be in the control of the people that own them. They must maintain that dominance, the same here and the same in Africa. We see it with Venezuela and Cuba. Our understanding of this scripture is often United States-based, but when you go to these other countries to give the sense, the people are fully aware of the robbing of their resources, and it must be brought to light.

“All these things are for good to the godly: so to the sinners they are turned into evil.” Because we have not repented, those things are turned over to the ungodly, and we will not reclaim them until the redeemer comes. In the meantime we must repent and keep the laws, statutes and commandments.

That is why “The bread of the needy is their life: he that defraudeth him thereof is a man of blood.” You think violence has to be a sword, a bomb or a bullet. Defraud people of those principal things and you are a man of blood. Economic violence is still violence. “He that taketh away his neighbour’s living slayeth him; and he that defraudeth the labourer of his hire is a bloodshedder.” Like the brother in the documentary who works all day and still has no money to eat: their only profit is labour.

Lamentations says the same: “We have drunken our water for money; our wood is sold unto us.” You see it now in Cuba, in Venezuela, in parts of Africa. Chains don’t have to be chains anymore.

precepts.text: The vision of dreams is the resemblance of one thing to another; the sheaf stood for Joseph and the sheaves for his brethren.
precepts.point: His brethren understood the dream, that he should reign over them, and hated him yet the more for his dreams and for his words.

note.label: Genesis 37: Joseph the Dreamer

precepts.why:
“The vision of dreams is the resemblance of one thing to another, even as the likeness of a face to a face.”

That is how to read Joseph's dream. The sheaf stood for Joseph and the sheaves for his brethren; one thing resembles another, as a face to a face. His brethren read it right: “Shalt thou indeed reign over us? or shalt thou indeed have dominion over us?” And they hated him yet the more.

precepts.text: The vision of dreams is the resemblance of one thing to another; the threes in both dreams stood for three days.
precepts.point: Both men saw variations of three, and in both dreams the three stood for three days. The dream is not always what is seen: the vision of dreams is the resemblance of one thing to another, even as the likeness of a face to a face. You may see yourself steal a piece of bread in a dream, and the meaning is that somebody will steal something from you in the days ahead; one thing resembles another.

note.label: Genesis 40: Do Not Interpretations Belong to God

precepts.why:
“The vision of dreams is the resemblance of one thing to another, even as the likeness of a face to a face.” A dream is not always what is seen; one thing resembles another. You may see yourself steal a piece of bread in a dream, and the meaning is that somebody will steal something from you in the days ahead.

So the chief baker’s “three white baskets” were not baskets: “The three baskets are three days.” The butler saw a variation of three and the baker saw a variation of three, and in both dreams the three stood for three days. The likeness was the same, but the ends were not: within three days Pharaoh would “lift up thy head from off thee, and shall hang thee on a tree; and the birds shall eat thy flesh from off thee.”

precepts.text: The vision of dreams is the resemblance of one thing to another; the sevens in Pharaoh's dreams resembled seven years.
precepts.point: His spirit was troubled, and none of the magicians and wise men of Egypt could interpret the dreams unto Pharaoh.

note.label: Genesis 41: Pharaoh's Dreams and Joseph's Rise Over Egypt

precepts.why:
“The vision of dreams is the resemblance of one thing to another, even as the likeness of a face to a face.” Pharaoh saw seven well favoured kine eaten up by seven ill favoured and leanfleshed kine, and seven rank and good ears devoured by seven thin ears “blasted with the east wind.” The kine were not kine and the ears were not ears; the sevens resembled seven years.

It is the same way the butler and the baker each saw a variation of three, and the three stood for three days. Pharaoh saw different variations of the number seven, and the dream was the resemblance of one thing to another. His spirit was troubled, and none of the magicians or wise men of Egypt could read that resemblance and interpret the dreams unto him.

precepts.text: He that taketh away his neighbour's living slayeth him.
precepts.point: Taking a man's tool takes away his living, like somebody stealing your tools so you cannot make a living. It is better that they steal your money, because with your tools you can go back and make more money.

note.label: Deuteronomy 24: Divorcement, Pledges, and Mercy to the Poor

precepts.why:
“No man shall take the nether or the upper millstone to pledge: for he taketh a man’s life to pledge.” Ecclesiasticus says how a tool is a man's life: “He that taketh away his neighbour’s living slayeth him; and he that defraudeth the labourer of his hire is a bloodshedder.”

Taking a man's tool takes away his living, like somebody stealing your tools so you cannot make a living. It is better that they steal your money, because with your tools you can go back and make more money; take the tools and the living is gone. That is why the millstone taken to pledge is a man's life taken to pledge.

precepts.text: The spoil was wrongfully gotten, taken against the will of the Lord, so the offering is ridiculous; all those animals were not going to pacify his anger.
precepts.point: Samuel makes it plain: Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams. Do you think the Lord prefers a sacrifice to atone for broken commandments over you simply keeping the commandments? That is a heavy verse.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

precepts.why:
“Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.” Do you think the Lord prefers a sacrifice to atone for broken commandments over you simply keeping the commandments? That is a heavy verse.

“He that sacrificeth of a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is ridiculous; and the gifts of unjust men are not accepted.” The spoil was wrongfully gotten, taken against the will of the Lord, so the offering is ridiculous. “The most High is not pleased with the offerings of the wicked; neither is he pacified for sin by the multitude of sacrifices.” All those animals were not going to pacify his anger.

precepts.text: The law is perfect, taking us into perfection with our lives.
precepts.point: The testimony of the Lord is sure because the prophecies in this Bible are sure; we have a more sure word of prophecy. Did we not go into slavery on ships like the Most High declared through Moses in Deuteronomy 28? We are living proof that the Bible is real.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul”. Ecclesiasticus says the same: “The law shall be found perfect without lies: and wisdom is perfection to a faithful mouth.”

The law is perfect, without lies. The law of the Lord being perfect means going into perfection with our lives: the law takes us there, and wisdom is perfection to a faithful mouth.
